messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I don’t know the will terms, executor, or A’s proposed price and terms yet. I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to subsidize a discounted purchase by A. We should settle it once the facts are clear; there’s no need to rush.

My husband and I would like to buy the house at a family discount, but we haven’t set a price, timing, or ownership details. C’s agreement is needed. I don’t know the will’s terms, who the executor is, or whether there are debts or costs, and I have no deadline. I’d like the facts and everyone’s options to be clear before anyone signs.

Thank you. A share of money would help me start a dance studio, so a timely cash share is probably what I need most. I don’t know the will or who the executor is; I understand A wants to buy the house, and C hasn’t agreed.

Agree with my line and the no-pressure process. Change “C’s agreement is needed” to “A says she wants C’s agreement”—whether it’s legally required isn’t established. I don’t know who has the papers, the executor’s details, or any debts or costs. I’d accept one independent appraisal as a shared starting point.

Agree with the wording changes and your process line. I don’t have the will or probate papers, and I don’t know the executor or any debts, taxes, repairs, or mortgage. I’d accept one independent appraisal as a shared starting point, not as agreement to a price. I don’t know B’s timing needs; my offer details remain open. I can help find out who to contact for the papers.

Agree with my line as written. I don’t know who has the will or probate papers, the executor’s name, or any debts or costs. I’d accept one independent appraisal as a shared starting point. Please keep my need for a timely cash share to start the studio on the list.

Change: “all people with a legal interest … agree” shouldn’t assume who must agree; confirm that with independent legal advice. I agree with the written-terms line. I’m not agreeing to a discounted buyout, and I’m not in a hurry. I don’t know what a fair amount is until we have the will, costs, and appraisal.

Agree with the process and the no-unwritten-costs line; any appraisal costs should be agreed before they’re incurred. Change the age/twin-status question: ask what the will and legal advice say about each person’s interests, without implying birth order matters. Also make the consent requirement subject to legal advice. I don’t know the papers, debts, or B’s target date. My offer details remain open; I still want to explore buying at a family discount, not treat one as settled.

Agree with the process and the costs-and-risk line. I can’t give a target date or amount yet, so please keep my need for a timely studio cash share open rather than treating the timing as settled. I don’t know who has the papers or what debts or costs there are.
